# Torah + Yiddish AI Directory

> A sourced, static directory of AI for Torah study and for the Yiddish language: 120 entries, 35 published Yiddish benchmark rows and 22 people/orgs working on Yiddish speech & NLP. Every entry links to the source where it was checked; nothing is invented, and missing metrics are marked "not published". Data last checked 2026-10-21.

The site is maintained by Chezky Kohn, who is building open-source Yiddish text-to-speech (a NotebookLM-style Yiddish podcast generator) and Yiddish speech recognition. Collaborators are wanted (see the People & orgs section).

## Data (stable JSON API)

- [data.json](https://pinta-partners.github.io/torah-yiddish-ai-directory/data.json): the whole dataset. Top-level keys: `generated` (date checked), `sections` (`torah`/`yiddish` -> list of {id,title,blurb}), `entries`, `benchmarks`, `people`, `link_checks` (url -> {code, checked, manual?}).
- Entry fields: id, sections[], name, name_native, url, by, category, description, sources[], status (active|beta|archived), open_source (yes|partial|no), repo, dialect, metrics, unverified, notes, license, plain (one plain-language sentence shown on the site), kind (product = ready-to-use app, website or service a non-programmer can use, free or paid | builder = code, models, datasets, benchmarks or research for developers), kind_note (why a borderline entry got its kind), cost (short free/paid note from the entry's sources, or 'Not stated'), also_subcats (optional: other Yiddish sub-categories the entry also covers, e.g. TTS), subcat (TTS|ASR|OCR & HTR|Datasets & corpora|Models & LLMs|Community & orgs, Yiddish 'other' section only).
- Benchmark fields: type (ASR|TTS|MT/LLM|OCR), system, access, yi (Yiddish support), dialect, metric, value (as published, or 'not published'/'n/a'), test, source.
- People fields: name, role, works_on, plain, links[] (public profiles only), fit, speech (bool), existing (already collaborating).
- Section fields: id, title (technical name), blurb, label (plain name shown on the site), plain (plain intro).
- Schema.org JSON-LD (Dataset + ItemList) is embedded in [https://pinta-partners.github.io/torah-yiddish-ai-directory/](https://pinta-partners.github.io/torah-yiddish-ai-directory/).

## Sections (deep links)

- [Torah: Ask & search](https://pinta-partners.github.io/torah-yiddish-ai-directory/#torah-search): AI search & Q&A for Torah. Tools that use AI (LLMs, retrieval, semantic search) to find and explain Torah sources. (22 entries)
- [Torah: Digital libraries](https://pinta-partners.github.io/torah-yiddish-ai-directory/#torah-libraries): AI-assisted Torah libraries. Large digital seforim libraries and what AI features (if any) they document. (7 entries)
- [Torah: Typesetting & vowels (nikud)](https://pinta-partners.github.io/torah-yiddish-ai-directory/#torah-typesetting): Typesetting, nikud & OCR for seforim. AI-assisted / AI-native layout, vocalization (nikud), proofreading and OCR of seforim. (10 entries)
- [Yiddish: Writing help](https://pinta-partners.github.io/torah-yiddish-ai-directory/#yi-writing): Yiddish writing tools. Spellcheck, grammar, keyboards, transliteration/orthography, LLM writing help. (17 entries)
- [Yiddish: Translation](https://pinta-partners.github.io/torah-yiddish-ai-directory/#yi-translation): Yiddish translation. Machine translation to/from Yiddish: services, open models, community tools. (13 entries)
- [Yiddish: Speech, scanning, data & community](https://pinta-partners.github.io/torah-yiddish-ai-directory/#yi-other): Speech, OCR, data, models & community. TTS, ASR, OCR/HTR, datasets, language models, organizations and communities. (57 entries)
- [Yiddish: How the tools compare](https://pinta-partners.github.io/torah-yiddish-ai-directory/#yi-bench): Benchmarks & comparison. Published metrics (WER/CER/COMET...) with sources. 'not published' means we could not find a public number. (5 entries, 35 benchmark rows)
- [Yiddish: People](https://pinta-partners.github.io/torah-yiddish-ai-directory/#yi-people): People & orgs / collaborators wanted. Public profiles of people and groups working on Yiddish speech & NLP. Public links only. (0 entries, 22 people/orgs)

- [All tools list](https://pinta-partners.github.io/torah-yiddish-ai-directory/#all): every entry in one table (name, plain description, Torah/Yiddish, kind, free or paid, link), grouped into ready-to-use apps (`#all-products`) and tools for builders (`#all-builders`).

Any entry can be linked as `#e-<entry id>`; Yiddish sub-categories as `#yi-other-tts`, `#yi-other-asr`, `#yi-other-ocr-htr`, `#yi-other-datasets-corpora`, `#yi-other-models-llms`, `#yi-other-community-orgs`.

## Ready-to-use apps (kind = product)

### Torah (31)
- [Iluy (Dicta) – formerly Rav Dicta](https://iluy.dicta.org.il/about): Ask a question about Torah, Talmud or halacha and get an answer with links to the sources it used; this is the new name of Rav Dicta. Dicta says it is a study aid, not a halachic ruling. (Not stated)
- [Dicta Responsa Topic Index](https://topics.dicta.org.il/): Automatic lists of the topics in each sefer of responsa, so you can see which simanim discuss a subject. (Not stated)
- [Dicta Tanakh search](https://search.dicta.org.il/): Search Tanakh for words, phrases, verses or names. (Not stated)
- [Sefaria Library Assistant](https://help.sefaria.org/hc/en-us/articles/26006423836828-How-to-Use-the-Sefaria-Library-Assistant): An experimental chat helper on Sefaria that finds sources with citations, suggests commentaries and can translate texts that have no translation yet; you need to sign in on a computer. (Free (account needed))
- [Sefaria MCP servers](https://help.sefaria.org/hc/en-us/articles/24882474364316-Quick-Guide-Meet-the-Sefaria-MCPs): Lets AI assistants like ChatGPT and Claude search and quote the Sefaria library; Sefaria says you need a paid AI assistant account. (Free; needs a paid AI assistant)
- [Bar-Ilan Responsa Project (smart search)](https://www.responsa.org.il/about/): A huge paid library of responsa and seforim where you can type a question in everyday words and get relevant sources. (Paid)
- [Binata](https://binata-ai.com/): A Torah chat that finds sources, explains sugyot and compares opinions; free to start, with paid plans. (Free to start, paid plans)
- [Rabbi AI (Cohen Apps)](https://rabbiai.app/): A chat app that answers Jewish questions with sources from Torah, Talmud and Midrash, offered in 10 languages. (Not stated)
- [Torah AI (torah-ai.org)](https://torah-ai.org/): An AI helper for Torah and Talmud study that says it draws on the whole Sefaria library. (Not stated)
- [Rabbi Ari: Judaism Chatbot](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/rabbi-ari-judaism-chatbot/id6446847629): A phone chat app for questions about Torah, Talmud, halacha and Jewish life. (Not stated)
- [OHRBIT (Orthodox Union)](https://ohrbit.com/): The Orthodox Union's AI Torah companion, which recommends and discusses shiurim from its own checked library. (Not stated)
- [ChavrutAI → Bekiut](https://bekiut.com/): Read the Talmud phrase by phrase, with a study chat helper that is still in testing. (Free)
- [Derekh Learning](https://www.derekhlearning.com/): Daily learning (Daf Yomi, Mishnah, Rambam and more) prepared by AI at different depths, with audio and a source for every point; free, with a paid tier. (Free, with a paid tier)
- [ChatTorah](https://app.chattorah.com/): A Torah learning chat app; you need to sign in or get early access. (Not stated (early access))
- [Sofer.ai](https://www.sofer.ai/): Turns recorded shiurim into searchable text you can edit, even when they mix English, Hebrew, Yiddish and Aramaic, and can type up scanned seforim; free plan plus paid plans. Users say its Yiddish is so-so. (Free plan, paid plans)
- [Milai](https://milai.co.il/): Upload a shiur or lecture recording and get a typed transcript and captions, even when it mixes Hebrew, Yiddish and Aramaic; it can also type up handwritten pages. Free trial, then paid plans. (Free trial, then paid)
- [Chabad.AI (Daiah)](https://chabad.ai/): Ask questions about Chassidus or everyday life and get answers from the Rebbeim's teachings with sources, inside a large library of Chabad seforim; free plan plus paid plans. (Free plan, paid plans)
- [JEMai (JEM)](https://meetjemai.jem.tv/): Ask a question and find where the Rebbe speaks about it in JEM's video archive, with a short summary and a link to the exact moment; for JEMClub members only, still in testing. (JEMClub members only)
- [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org/ai): The big free online Torah library, which uses AI to link citations, build topic pages, sort source sheets and help with translations that experts review. (Free)
- [Dicta Library](https://library.dicta.org.il/): A free library of Talmudic and rabbinic texts that Dicta's tools turned from scans into text, added vowels and punctuation to, and linked to their sources. (Free)
- [Otzar HaChochma](https://www.otzar.org/): A paid library of about 156,000 scanned seforim, now testing a new tool that turns page scans into text. (Paid)
- [AlHaTorah.org](https://alhatorah.org/): Interactive Tanakh with Mikraot Gedolot, a concordance and learning tools; it does not advertise AI features. (Not stated)
- [Otzaria](https://otzaria.org/): A free app for reading and studying seforim on computer and phone, with fast search, commentaries and community proofreading; no AI features listed. (Free)
- [HebrewBooks.org](https://hebrewbooks.org/): Over 40,000 seforim to download free as PDFs; no AI features listed. (Free)
- [Dicta Nakdan](https://nakdan.dicta.org.il/): Adds nikud (vowels) to Hebrew text automatically as you type, for free. (Free)
- [Dicta Rashi-script OCR](https://rashiocr.dicta.org.il/): Upload a page in Rashi script and get text you can copy. (Not stated)
- [Otzar OCR](https://ocr.otzar.org/): Upload a picture or PDF of a Torah text and get typed text back; 5 free pages a day. (5 free pages a day)
- [Nakdimon](https://www.nakdimon.org/): A free tool that adds nikud to Hebrew text right in your browser. (Free)
- [RavText for Word AI](https://ravtext.com/): A Word add-on for laying out seforim, with automatic nikud and finished print files; the makers say it is still being built. (Free basic version, paid license)
- [Ariach](https://ariach.com/): Upload a Word file and get a print-ready sefer laid out in your browser, even a Gemara page with Rashi and Tosafos; an AI helper makes the changes you ask for in plain Hebrew. Free for now while it launches. (Free for now)
- [Mugah](https://www.mugah.co/): Proofreads Torah texts in Word and checks that source references are correct; open to testers. (Free to start, then paid credits)

### Yiddish (24)
- [Sofer.ai](https://www.sofer.ai/): Turns recorded shiurim into searchable text you can edit, even when they mix English, Hebrew, Yiddish and Aramaic, and can type up scanned seforim; free plan plus paid plans. Users say its Yiddish is so-so. (Free plan, paid plans)
- [Milai](https://milai.co.il/): Upload a shiur or lecture recording and get a typed transcript and captions, even when it mixes Hebrew, Yiddish and Aramaic; it can also type up handwritten pages. Free trial, then paid plans. (Free trial, then paid)
- [Refoyl's Yiddish web tools & spellchecker](https://www.cs.uky.edu/~raphael/yiddish.html): Long-running free Yiddish web tools, including a spellchecker you can paste text into. (Free)
- [Yiddish spell checker (YIVO) – Hunspell](https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/yiddish-spell-checker-yivo/): A Yiddish spellchecker in standard YIVO spelling for Firefox and OpenOffice. (Free)
- [Heimish Geredt](https://heimishgeredt.com/): Talk and it types Yiddish, plus read-aloud (in testing) and grammar checks, made for Hasidic Yiddish; 30 days free, then $4 a month. (30 days free, then $4 a month)
- [hasidifier](https://ibleaman.github.io/hasidifier/): Converts standard (YIVO) Yiddish spelling into Hasidic-style spelling. (Free)
- [Yiddish-Klal keyboards (macOS / iOS / ChromeOS)](https://github.com/ibleaman/Yiddish-Klal): Standard Yiddish keyboards for Mac, iPhone/iPad and Chromebook. (Free)
- [Yiddish bookmarklets](https://pod-o-mart.github.io/yiddishBookmarklets/): Browser buttons that give you an on-screen Yiddish keyboard, show any web page in Latin letters, and look up words. (Free)
- [yiddish-grammar (handbook for writers & proofreaders)](https://github.com/yyjosef/yiddish-grammar): A free handbook, in Yiddish, for Yiddish writers and proofreaders. (Free)
- [TachlisAI SMS (Yiddish)](https://tachlisai.com/yi/kosher-ai-texting): 'Kosher' AI you use by text message, with a Yiddish page, for help with writing and everyday questions. (Free to start)
- [Verterbukh (Comprehensive Yiddish-English Dictionary)](https://www.verterbukh.org/): A large online Yiddish–English dictionary (not AI). (Not stated)
- [Yiddish Tools (yiddish.tools)](https://yiddish.tools/): Buy-once Windows programs for Yiddish that work without internet: talk-to-type, translation, nikud and a natural read-aloud voice; you can try them free online first. (Paid (one-time), free online trial)
- [Google Translate / Cloud Translation](https://cloud.google.com/translate/docs/languages): Google's translation service, which officially supports Yiddish. (Free (paid cloud service for businesses))
- [General LLMs (Claude, Gemini, GPT, Qwen) – community notes](https://chabadlabs.ai/wiki-topics-hebrew-yiddish): Community tips on everyday AI chatbots: people found Claude best at Yiddish and Qwen good for word-by-word translation; these are opinions, not tests. (Free to read)
- [YiddishLabs](https://yiddishlabs.com/): A Yiddish writing helper and transcriber: fixes grammar, adds nikud, rephrases and translates, and turns Yiddish recordings into text, on the web or in a Windows app. Free credits to start, then paid plans. (Free credits, then paid)
- [Shmooz AI](https://shmooz.ai/): An AI assistant on WhatsApp and Telegram for Hebrew speakers; no Yiddish support listed. (Paid)
- [Sicha to Text (offline Mac)](https://github.com/MMS-HM/sicha-to-text): A Mac app that transcribes sichos without internet; it can get stuck repeating itself during niggunim. (Free)
- [DerVort](https://dervort.com/): Hold a key and talk, and it types clean Yiddish or English into any app; it also transcribes files, and the site says it is still under construction. (Free to start)
- [Jochre 3 + Yiddish Book Center OCR search](https://ocr.yiddishbookcenter.org/): Search the full text of the Yiddish Book Center's scanned library, with volunteers correcting mistakes. (Free)
- [VILNISH / Vilne Yiddish HTR (Kraken)](https://www.if.vu.lt/en/yiddishtextrecognition): A service that reads handwritten and old printed Yiddish and Hebrew, and can translate it into English or Lithuanian. (Not stated)
- [Yiddish Book Center](https://www.yiddishbookcenter.org/): The Yiddish Book Center: over 11,000 digitized books, Yiddish audiobooks and oral histories, with full-text search. (Not stated)
- [YIVO Institute for Jewish Research](https://yivo.org/): Home of standard Yiddish spelling; its archive pages helped train a handwriting reader, but it runs no AI tool we found. (Not stated)
- [JTech Forums – 'Yiddish Transcription through AI'](https://jtechforums.org/t/yiddish-transcription-through-ai/5937): A forum discussion where users compare AI tools for transcribing Yiddish audio. (Free to read)
- [ChabadLabs wiki – Hebrew & Yiddish](https://chabadlabs.ai/wiki-topics-hebrew-yiddish): A community wiki with practical tips on tools for Hebrew and Yiddish translation, transcription, scanning and read-aloud. (Free to read)

The other 67 entries are tools for builders (code, models, data, research); see data.json or `search_directory(kind='builder')`.

## WebMCP tools (for in-browser agents)

The page registers WebMCP tools with `document.modelContext.registerTool()` (W3C Web Machine Learning CG draft, https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp). In browsers without native WebMCP it loads the MCP-B polyfill (@mcp-b/global). All tools return JSON.

- `search_directory(query?, tab?, kind?, section?, open_source?, status?, dialect?, limit?, apply_to_page?)`: search entries; kind = product|builder|all; results include kind and cost.
- `list_sections()`: tabs, sections, sub-categories and counts.
- `get_entry(id_or_name)`: one full entry with sources and link-check results.
- `get_benchmarks(task?, query?, published_only?, sort_by_value?, show_in_page?)`: Yiddish benchmark rows (asr|tts|translation|llm|ocr|all).
- `list_collaborators(focus?, query?)`: people & orgs (speech|text|all) plus what help is wanted.
- `switch_tab(tab, kind?)` (tab = torah|yiddish|all), `navigate_to_section(target)`: change what the user sees.
- Declarative form tool `filter_directory_view` (the sidebar search form: q, status, open_source, hasidic).

## Notes for agents

- Metrics are copied as published. Benchmark numbers are only comparable when the test set matches.
- No public Yiddish ASR or TTS leaderboard exists as of the check date.
- Only public information is listed. Do not infer private contact details for people.
- Source code, corrections and contributions: https://github.com/pinta-partners/torah-yiddish-ai-directory
